question: Why is a Vernier height gauge preferred over a simple steel rule for height 8 measurement?

options.text: It is cheaper than steel rule.
It does not require a surface plate.

solution:
The correct answer is __It provides more precise measurements.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A Vernier height gauge__ is a tool used for accurate height measurement in industrial and laboratory settings.
 
• Unlike a simple steel rule, it allows measurements with precision to fractions of a millimeter.
 
• It is equipped with a Vernier scale, which enables highly detailed readings.
 
• It requires a flat surface or surface plate to ensure accuracy during measurement.
 
• Vernier height gauges are commonly used for tool setting, layout work, and quality inspection tasks.
 
• They are particularly helpful for applications where precision is critical, such as in engineering or manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Steel Rule:**

 
 
• A basic measuring tool used for linear measurements.
 
• It lacks the precision of a Vernier scale and is more prone to human error.
 
 
 
• **Surface Plate:**
 
 
• A flat reference surface used in precision measurement.
 
• It ensures the stability and accuracy of measurements taken with tools like the Vernier height gauge.
 
 
 
• **Digital Height Gauge:**
 
 
• A more advanced version of the Vernier height gauge with a digital display.
 
• It provides quicker and easier readings but is generally more expensive.
